Urgent Safety Hazard at English Muffin Way and Tennison Drive - No Temp Stop Lines after Repaving

I am writing to report an extremely dangerous traffic condition at the four-way stop at English Muffin Way and Tennison Drive in Frederick County.

English Muffin Way was recently repaved, but the stop lines for eastbound and westbound traffic have not yet been restored. Because English Muffin Way is four lanes wide and the stop signs are positioned far from the lanes of travel, drivers are frequently failing to recognize that they must stop without the pavement markings.

During the past six days, I have personally been nearly broadsided three times while turning from Tennison Drive because vehicles traveled through the intersection at approximately 40 mph without stopping.  One of which included a fully loaded dump truck. Today, I also witnessed a tractor-trailer traveling westbound on English Muffin Way miss the stop sign, brake hard, and finally stop in the middle of the intersection.

This intersection was already dangerous before the repaving, with drivers regularly failing to stop on English Muffin Way. Without visible stop lines, the condition has become an immediate and serious hazard.

I understand that installing permanent pavement markings may require additional time. However, I respectfully request that temporary stop lines or other highly visible temporary markings be installed immediately. Waiting for the permanent markings creates an unacceptable risk of a serious collision. 

Longer term, the County should evaluate additional safety improvements at this intersection. These could include relocating the stop signs closer to the lanes of travel, adding “STOP AHEAD” pavement markings in the eastbound and westbound lanes, and installing flashing red LED borders or warning lights around the stop signs.
Residents of the Wellington Trace area know to exercise extreme caution at this intersection because of the longstanding pattern of drivers failing to stop on English Muffin Way. Drivers unfamiliar with the area may not recognize the danger until it is too late. Given the current absence of pavement markings and the heavy commercial truck traffic—including dump trucks and tractor-trailers—the risk of serious injury or, God forbid, a fatality is unacceptably high. With school starting in less than two weeks, buses and student that attend the elementary school off of Tennison Drive are especially at risk.

Please treat this as an urgent public-safety matter and advise when temporary markings will be installed and whether the County will evaluate longer-term improvements to the intersection.

Thank you
issues.address: English Muffin Way & Tennison Dr Ballenger Creek, MD, 21703, USA
